;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Kabul gurdwara attack]]
***Gunmen kill 25 worshippers at a [[gurdwara]] in [[Kabul]], [[Afghanistan]]. [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant – Khorasan Province|ISIL]] claims responsibility. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-afghanistan-attack/gunmen-in-afghanistan-kill-25-at-sikh-complex-islamic-state-claims-responsibility-idUKKBN21C0IG (Reuters)]
*[[Libyan Civil War (2014–present)|Libyan Civil War]]
**[[2019–20 Western Libya offensive]]
***Forces loyal to the [[Government of National Accord|GNA]] assault the [[Okba Ibn Nafa Air Base]], west of [[Tripoli, Libya|Tripoli]], while the [[Libyan National Army]] captures several towns near the [[Berber languages|Berber]] city of [[Zuwarah]], including [[Zaltan]], [[Jumayl, Libya|Jumayl]] and [[Ras Ajdir]]. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-libya-security/libya-battles-escalate-as-coronavirus-arrives-in-country-idUKKBN21C1FU (Reuters)]

;Arts and culture
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Egypt]]
***[[Egypt]] begins disinfection on the [[Giza pyramid complex]] as an effort to contain [[COVID-19]]. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-health-coronavirus-egypt-pyramids/egypt-deep-cleans-pyramids-site-emptied-of-tourists-idUKKBN21C2FH (Reuters)]
**[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on cinema]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China]]
***[[China]] announces that ''[[The Avengers (2012 film)|The Avengers]]'', ''[[Avengers: Age of Ultron]]'', ''[[Avengers: Infinity War]]'', ''[[Avengers: Endgame]]'', ''[[Avatar (2009 film)|Avatar]]'', ''[[Inception]]'', and ''[[Interstellar (film)|Interstellar]]'' will be re-released in theaters following the end of their [[2020 Hubei lockdowns|lockdowns]] as a hope to revive their cinemas. [https://www.cnet.com/news/china-is-re-releasing-avengers-and-avatar-to-revive-cinemas-after-the-coronavirus/ (CNET)]

;Business and economy
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
**The [[United States Senate]] and the [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] reaches a [[CARES Act|$2 trillion stimulus package deal]] following talks with [[United States Secretary of the Treasury|Treasury Secretary]] [[Steven Mnuchin]]. The bill passes, and is expected to go to the [[United States House of Representatives]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2020/03/25/trump-senate-coronavirus-economic-stimulus-2-trillion/ (''The Washington Post'')] [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/03/25/senate-passes-2-trillion-coronavirus-stimulus-package.html (CNBC)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Kuril Islands earthquake]]
**A magnitude 7.5 [[earthquake]] hits the [[Kuril Islands]] town [[Severo-Kurilsk]] in [[Russia]]'s [[Russian Far East|Far East]]. [https://www.newsweek.com/major-magnitude-7-5-earthquake-russia-kuril-islands-1494120 (''Newsweek'')]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****​[[India]] goes under a [[2020 India coronavirus lockdown|nationwide lockdown]] to contain the coronavirus pandemic. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-india-52024239 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Palestinian territories]]
****[[State of Palestine|Palestine]] reports its first death from COVID-19 in the [[West Bank]], the patient was a woman in her 60s. [https://english.alaraby.co.uk/english/news/2020/3/25/palestine-reports-its-first-coronavirus-related-death (''The New Arab'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****The [[United States]] has its deadliest COVID-19 day to date, with 223 related deaths. [https://www.cnn.com/world/live-news/coronavirus-outbreak-03-25-20-intl-hnk/h_215e6b9339a992b24b624a15c13dcca2 (CNN)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)]]
*****[[New York City]] records 81 more deaths from COVID-19, bringing the city's death toll to 280. [[Mayor of New York City|Mayor]] [[Bill de Blasio]] has warned that more than half of all New Yorkers could become infected.  [https://nypost.com/2020/03/25/nyc-sees-81-coronavirus-deaths-in-one-day/ (''New York Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]
****[[New Zealand]] declares a national [[state of emergency]] as the number of confirmed COVID-19 cases rise to 205. [https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?objectid=12319699 (''New Zealand Herald'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Solomon Islands]]
****[[Solomon Islands]] declare state of emergency due to COVID-19. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/412607/solomons-declare-state-of-public-emergency-because-of-covid-19 (RNZ)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Samoa]]
****[[Prime Minister of Samoa|Samoan Prime Minister]] [[Tuilaʻepa Saʻilele Malielegaoi|Tuilaepa Aiono Sailele Malielegaoi]] announces that people will be fined for breaking the new restrictions of movement due COVID-19. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/412587/samoa-to-fine-people-who-don-t-adhere-to-covid-19-restrictions (RNZ)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary]]
****The [[Foreign and Commonwealth Office]] confirms that Steven Dick, a 37-year-old [[diplomat]] to their mission in [[Budapest]], has died from COVID-19. [https://news.yahoo.com/steven-dick-deputy-head-mission-171521800.html (Yahoo News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****[[Spain]] surpasses China in the number of COVID-19-related deaths and becomes the country with the second-most deaths, after an increase of 738 in a single day. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/coronavirus-spain-death-toll-china-cases-how-many-covid-19-a9423981.html (''Independent'')]
****[[First Deputy Prime Minister of Spain|First Deputy Prime Minister]] [[Carmen Calvo]] tests positive for COVID-19. She was admitted to hospital on Sunday and becomes the third member of the [[Government of Spain|Spanish government]] to be diagnosed with the virus. [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/03/25/spains-deputy-pm-carmen-calvo-tests-positive-for-coronavirus.html (CNBC)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[Charles, Prince of Wales]] tests positive for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] while [[Camilla, Duchess of Cornwall]] tests negative; both now self-isolate due to the health classifications. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-52033845 (BBC News)]
****The first death from COVID-19 is confirmed in the [[Channel Islands]], an elderly patient at a hospital in [[Jersey]]. [https://www.itv.com/news/channel/2020-03-26/first-coronavirus-death-in-channel-islands/ (ITV News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****[[President of France|President]] [[Emmanuel Macron]] announces the launch of military {{ill|Operation Résilience|qid=Q88592402}} and investments in their [[Health care in France|health system]] in an attempt to fight COVID-19. [https://www.france24.com/en/20200325-macron-launches-army-operation-resilience-to-support-fight-against-coronavirus (France 24)] [https://www.euronews.com/2020/03/25/france-s-macron-announces-military-operation-and-hospital-investment-plan-to-fight-covid-1 (Euronews)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mali]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Guinea-Bissau]]
****The first COVID-19 cases are confirmed in [[Mali]] and [[Guinea-Bissau]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/mali-guinea-bissau-confirm-1st-coronavirus-cases/1779246 (Anadolu Agency)]

;Law and crime
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
**[[President of the Philippines|President]] [[Rodrigo Duterte]] signs a law granting him special temporary powers to direct the operations of private hospitals and take over [[Transportation in the Philippines|public transportation]]. [https://www.npr.org/sections/coronavirus-live-updates/2020/03/24/820906636/concerns-in-philippines-after-duterte-given-emergency-powers-to-fight-covid-19-s (NPR)]
*[[Assassination of Jamal Khashoggi]], [[Saudi Arabia–Turkey relations]]
**[[Turkey]] indicts 20 [[Saudis]] for the assassination of [[Jamal Khashoggi]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/03/25/world/europe/turkey-jamal-khashoggi-saudis.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[Transportation in Dubai]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Arab Emirates]]
**[[Dubai]] lifts their ban on trucks weighing 2.5 tonnes as an effort to contain COVID-19. [https://gulfnews.com/amp/uae/transport/coronavirus-dubai-temporarily-lifts-ban-on-movement-of-trucks-1.70618893 (''Gulf News'')]
*Former [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Ukraine)|Foreign Minister]] [[Leonid Kozhara]] is arrested by security forces on charges of [[Homicide|murdering]] advertising mogul [[Sergiy Starytsky]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/ukraines-ex-foreign-minister-arrested-for-murder/a-52918176 (Deutsche Welle)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Russian constitutional referendum]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
**[[President of Russia|President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] postpones a referendum on constitutional changes that could extend his time in office for two more six-year terms because of the COVID-19 pandemic. Putin's current term runs through 2024. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-52038814 (BBC News)]
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on politics]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ohio]]
****The [[Ohio Senate]] passes a coronavirus relief bill, which includes extending [[Postal voting|mail-in voting]] for the [[2020 Ohio Democratic primary|Ohio primary]] by April 28. [https://www.cleveland.com/open/2020/03/ohio-senate-passes-coronavirus-relief-bill-extending-primary-voting-until-april-28-waiving-school-testing-requirements.html (Cleveland.com)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kosovo]], [[Government of Kosovo]]
*** A [[motion of no confidence]] filed by junior coalition partner [[Democratic League of Kosovo]] (LDK) against [[Prime Minister of Kosovo|Prime Minister]] [[Albin Kurti]] passes with 82—32 votes, toppling the [[Kurti cabinet]]. [[Vetëvendosje]] now has 15 days to nominate a new Prime Minister. [https://www.dw.com/en/kosovos-government-toppled-through-no-confidence-vote-over-coronavirus-response/a-52919171 (Deutsche Welle)] [https://indianexpress.com/article/coronavirus/kosovo-government-coronavirus-us-6332086/ (''The New York Times'' via The Indian Express)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/mar/26/kosovo-government-falls-in-vote-of-no-confidence (''The Guardian'')]
